title: Building Council: A Multi-Model AI Deliberation Engine
excerpt: A look inside Council, our open-source multi-model AI deliberation framework. We built it to orchestrate conversations between specialist LLM agents — each with distinct personas — then aggregate their responses through confidence-weighted voting. Here's how it works and why we use it daily.
author: Matthew Goodwin

title: RedSync v1.0.14 — Proximity Voice Chat & Stability Overhaul
excerpt: RedSync 1.0.14 is here with a major proximity voice chat overhaul, improved server stability under high player counts, and a new auto-healing watchdog that detects and restarts hung game sessions without player interruption.
author: Matthew Goodwin

title: Blackwall Studio Is Live
excerpt: We are officially launching Blackwall Studio — a multiplayer game development studio dedicated to extending the lives of games. Our first release: the full studio website and a new org profile on GitHub. RedSync development continues at full speed.
author: Matthew Goodwin

title: RedSync v1.0.13 — New Events & Stability
excerpt: RedSync 1.0.13 is out with new proximity voice chat improvements, Project Smasher combat event refinements, and dedicated server stability patches. The anti-regression watchdog now auto-rolls back bad updates before players are affected.
author: Matthew Goodwin

title: Council & Synapse Tools Released as Open Source
excerpt: We have open-sourced two internal tools: Council, a multi-model AI deliberation engine, and Synapse, a reverse engineering workbench with HexStrike AI. Both are available now on our GitHub under the MIT license.
author: Anthony Wells

title: Inside the Netcode: Building RedSync from Scratch
excerpt: A deep dive into how we built RedSync's networking layer from the ground up — from reverse engineering Cyberpunk 2077's game state to building a custom C++ synchronization core with GameNetworkingSockets.
author: Matthew Goodwin

title: Crafting the Blackwall Studio Aesthetic: Glitch Text & CRT Effects
excerpt: A behind-the-scenes look at how we built the Cyberpunk-inspired visual effects for blackwallstudio.com — CSS-only glitch text with stepped keyframe offsets, chromatic aberration on hover, CRT scan line overlays, and a breathing logo pulse. All in vanilla CSS, no JavaScript animation libraries.
author: Matthew Goodwin
